messages:
olivia: follow-up from yesterday's RFC: proposing we separate soft-eviction timing from pin lifetime by introducing an explicit 'grace token' (eviction_grace). goal: make fairness and GC reasoning simpler and avoid pins implicitly prolonging eviction windows across tenants.

sam: sounds useful. what would the API change look like? small header or new call?

olivia: minimal: optional field on AcquirePin/ReleasePin -> eviction_grace (string). runtime tracks a tiny grace record by id; pins control immediate protection, grace controls soft->hard demote timing. AcquirePin(prefix, pin_id, eviction_grace="gr-42").

mike: can grace outlive pins? i.e., token stays after pins released? potential for accumulating stale tokens. we'll need GC.

olivia: yes, grace can outlive pins intentionally. plan: TTL-based GC with refresh on any use. GC after TTL + safety slack. expose telemetry for count and GC lag.

aina: handoff implications: when prefix moves, how does the new owner learn about active grace tokens? do we add a central service?

olivia: two paths: piggyback token state in handoff RPC (preferred short-term), or have a small central reconcile endpoint for misses. piggyback keeps things local and fast.

sam: piggyback is easier but may miss in multi-region/private setups. hybrid approach: piggyback + optional reconcile for rare misses.

mike: invariants to protect: 1) pins prevent any eviction, 2) grace only delays hard demote, never prevents a pin from protecting, 3) handoff must be idempotent.

olivia: agreed. enforcement: eviction flow checks pin_count==0 AND grace_expired before allowing hard demote. pins still beat grace.

jean: concurrency hazard: concurrent grace refreshes and clock skew could cause premature GC. need monotonic versioning on grace records.

olivia: implement grace record = id + epoch + last_refresh_ts + origin. refresh bumps epoch and writes monotonic counter into local handoff log; handoff transfers epoch. prevents stale overwrites.

aina: telemetry / alerts to add: active_grace_count, mean_grace_age, grace_gc_delay, handoff_grace_misses, evict_blocked_by_grace. helps validate canary.

olivia: rollout: opt-in node flag enable_eviction_grace. start on internal dev cluster with prefix-heavy workloads. monitor GC growth + miss rate.

sam: SDK compatibility: add optional field, default empty. no breaking changes unless customers opt in.

mike: perf/storage: extra check on eviction path (cheap). storage: one tiny record per active grace token. still, add soft cap per-shard and LRU on grace ids when exceeding thresholds.

olivia: open questions: TTL value (suggest 30s), safety margin (10s), cross-cluster transferability (start single-cluster), and an admin override to force-expire grace for ops.

jean: admin override + debug endpoint that enumerates grace tokens per-prefix is really helpful for oncall.

aina: I'll write a short follow-up RFC with API snippets, canary checklist, and migration notes. include telemetry dashboard templates.

olivia: I'll open the RFC PR and link the infra ticket. tagging @infra-bot for canary infra.

infra-bot: created INFRA-1098 for canary cluster and resource allocation (assigned to eng-runtime on-call).

sam: minor: keep ReleasePin semantics unchanged in presence of grace.

olivia: yep backwards-compatible. ship opt-in, document in /docs/runtime/eviction.md.

mike: :+1: let's watch the first week metrics closely; roll back if grace GC grows unexpectedly or handoff misses spike.
